geography: World Bank countries and economies with a non-aggregate region and at least one published value in the series. Codes follow the World Bank registry, including XKX for Kosovo.
transformations: Rows are grouped under their source economy codes. All years within the observed series span appear. Null in JSON and blank in CSV represent an unavailable observation. Numeric values retain the precision returned by the publisher. Explicit zeros and status codes are retained.
validation: All country-year values and missing observations were compared to the separate official bulk CSV. One near-zero natural gas estimate for Cameroon in 2013 has more decimal places in the bulk CSV. Rounding that value to the API precision gives exactly the API value. Both published decimals appear in the series metadata. The explorer retains the API value.

resource-rent-coal.name: Coal rents (% of GDP)
resource-rent-coal.definition: Coal rents are the difference between the value of both hard and soft coal production at world prices and their total costs of production.

resource-rent-forest.name: Forest rents (% of GDP)
resource-rent-forest.definition: Forest rents are roundwood harvest times the product of regional prices and a regional rental rate.

resource-rent-mineral.definition: Mineral rents are the difference between the value of production for a stock of minerals at world prices and their total costs of production. Minerals included in the calculation are tin, gold, lead, zinc, iron, copper, nickel, silver, bauxite, and phosphate.

methodology.source: World Bank, The Changing Wealth of Nations, distributed in World Development Indicators.
methodology.interpretation: The total and component series are retained independently. A missing component or total stays blank. Each series represents an annual monetary estimate. The rent denominator is GDP and the depletion denominator is gross national income (GNI).
methodology.measure: The estimates cover oil, natural gas, coal, minerals and forests. Extraction rents use commodity prices and estimated production costs. Forest rents use roundwood harvest, regional prices and a regional rental rate. The percentage measures economic rent rather than government receipts or export revenue.
